title: The Wild Choir Again
premise: Dominic Coldharbour has spent her life in the valley of Vell, where the wards suppress all magic and her gift for speaking with beasts marks her for death under the Choir's law. When the wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns Vell was never a refuge but a cage built by the Choir to hide their stolen power, and that the beasts she's always understood are the wards' living anchors. Hunted by the Choir's inquisitors and guided by a disgraced ex-warden named Sable, Dominic must reach the Door at the heart of the dead country and decide whether to restore the old order or unmake it. In the end she refuses both: she sings the wild choir herself, scattering the Choir's hoarded magic back into beast and human alike, and walks out of Vell as its first free citizen rather than its queen.
about_author: Isandro Almeida is the pen name of a former field biologist who spent six years recording birdsong in remote mountain valleys before turning to fantasy. They write about outsiders who talk to animals because, they insist, the animals usually answer first.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the eve of the valley's Founding Festival, Dominic secretly heals a wounded wolf with whispered speech, then watches every star above Vell go dark while the border wards shatter like glass. The emotional beat is dread disguised as wonder: the sky breaking open mirrors the secret she can no longer contain.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The village elders impose curfew and blame 'wild magic,' but the beasts grow frantic, telling Dominic the wards didn't fail—they were taken. She finds a dying ward-stag whose last words name the Choir. Beat: the comfort of home curdles into the realization that her whole life was a lie of geography.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Sheepfold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A one-armed woman in torn warden grey collapses at the Coldharbour farm, pursued by something that leaves no tracks. Sable recognizes what Dominic is on sight—and chooses not to report her. Beat: wary alliance; two people who have survived by hiding recognize each other.

chapters.title: The Choir Comes Singing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inquisitors arrive in white robes, singing harmonies that make villagers weep and confess invented sins. They execute the miller's son for 'beast-taint' he never had. Dominic, hidden in the hayloft, understands silence is complicity. Beat: grief hardening into resolve; justice outside the law becomes personal.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic, Sable, and the wolf Bracken slip through the broken border into a country where maps have stopped working—roads loop, towns remember different names. Sable reveals the Choir hoards magic in a vault called the Door. Beat: vertigo and exhilaration; freedom feels indistinguishable from being lost.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the capital Ashfall, they find survivors worshipping the vanished stars, led by a gentle priest who was once Sable's warden commander. He offers sanctuary—at the price of Dominic's gift, 'surrendered to the Choir for safekeeping.' Beat: temptation; belonging offered as a trap.

chapters.title: Beasts at the Gate
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Choir captures Sable, and Dominic does the unthinkable: she calls every creature in Ashfall—rats, ravens, the city's half-starved dogs—to rise. The rescue succeeds messily, and she sees her own reflection in a shattered window: someone powerful, and frightened of it. Beat: power's first taste, and its first cost—a child trampled in the chaos.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Guided by Bracken and the ghost-memory of the ward-stag, they reach the Door beneath the mountains: a vault where the Choir keeps magic caged in singing crystal, and where the stolen stars are stored as seeds of light. Sable confesses she once guarded it and looked away from its cruelty. Beat: confrontation with complicity—the corruption isn't one villain but an appetite everyone fed.

chapters.title: The Wild Choir
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Climax. The Choir's High Cantor offers Dominic a place beside him: order, safety, a world where nothing wild needs fearing. Instead she opens the vault and sings—not alone, but with every beast she has ever spoken to, a chord no single voice could hold. The stars scatter back into the sky; magic floods loose. Beat: refusal of corrupted power; belonging chosen over safety.

chapters.title: First Citizen
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue tone. Vell rebuilds without wards or walls; some neighbors forgive her, some never will, and she accepts both. Sable takes up honest road-work, Bracken grows old slowly, and the new stars include one that answers when spoken to. Final beat: quiet resolution—home is no longer a place you're trapped in, but one you choose daily.
